coordinates.locator: geometry:chooz-far-laboratory (two-circle intersection of the TDR baselines about the B1/B2 unit centroids)
coordinates.note: Derived, not published: the far laboratory is placed where the Double Chooz baselines (1114.6 m and 997.9 m) meet, choosing the solution under the hill near Chooz A. If the TDR's RE/RW labels were geographic the point would move about 1.6 km; the method is described in the geometry record.

depth_mwe.quote: Both detectors were in underground laboratories with shielding against cosmic radiation of 120 m w.e. in the near and 300 m w.e. in the far detector.

name: Double Chooz far detector site
notes: The Double Chooz far detector was installed in the existing underground laboratory of the original CHOOZ experiment (collaboration's 2022 detector paper), at 1050 m from the reactor cores (2012 discovery paper's abstract).

summary.plain: A hall inside a hill near the Chooz nuclear plant in France, over a kilometre from the reactors, shielded by rock from cosmic rays.
summary.technical: Double Chooz far-detector hall, 1050 m from the Chooz-B reactor cores, under ~300 m.w.e. of rock shielding.
